summary: The note-candidates Dreamer pass now writes down a plan one person has stated when it has an unsettled corner, and reads a plan buried in ordinary talk; its doctrine is rewritten for what the Dreamer is now (a tool-free judge) instead of the research register that pushed it toward an empty answer. A live scenario suite measures the pass against the deployed model.
details: First live fire (2026-09-08 02:19 HKT) on a real dated arrangement with two open corners returned `{"candidates": []}`. The trace showed the batch was exactly that one message and the prompt was the deployed doctrine + objective (c9a73442). An offline probe of the same message across five prompt variants showed the prompt, not the pipeline, was the bottleneck.

`evals/cases/note_candidates/note_candidates.yaml` + `evals/note_candidates.py` + `evals.run --suite note_candidates`: ten batches (five must create/update a note, five must not) driven N times through the REAL `DreamerRuntime` + `NoteCandidateAdaptor` over `InMemoryNoteStore` with only the model live (`nora.app.eval_support.run_note_candidates_case`), graded structurally on the notebook — a note created, a head revised, or nothing — never by a judge; `unavailable` is ERROR, apart from FAIL. `--dreamer-dir` measures a prompt variant held as files and the run reports the instruction hash; `--model` names the deployed OmniRoute alias from a dev machine. `make eval-note-candidates`.

Measured against `nora-dreamer` / reasoning none, 3 samples per case: as-deployed prompt precision 1.00 recall 0.60 (8/10); objective addition alone 1.00 / 0.87 (10/10); judge doctrine alone 1.00 / 0.67 (9/10); both 1.00 / 0.93 (10/10). No variant produced a false note on any of the fifteen negative samples.

`nora/dreamer/objectives/note-candidates.md` is version 2: a stated plan with an unsettled corner is a notebook entry even before anyone replies; read the whole batch for the arrangement, not its mood; resolve a relative date against the message's own timestamp. `nora/dreamer/doctrine/dreamer.md` is version 2: the research register (sources, pages, when to stop looking) is gone; the two ways to be wrong — cluttering the notebook and missing what the room is in the middle of — are stated as both costing.
Both files are bind-mounted and hot-reload per run: this change is live on the next `note-candidates` fire after the checkout on the host is pulled, with no rebuild.
limitations: Three to five samples per case at temperature 0.7 is enough to rank the variants and not enough to put a confidence interval on recall; the one-person stated plan still misses roughly one sample in three under the shipped prompt.
The suite grades what the notebook holds, not whether the body is any good — reading created bodies by eye is the next step design 37 §7 names.
The suite runs the pass over `InMemoryNoteStore`, so it cannot see a defect that lives only in `SqlNoteStore`; the note store contract suite is what covers that seam.
